subject.title: [Feature Request]: one-line local bootstrap for daemon + dashboard auth + Telegram owner setup

question: Should OpenClaw add a first-class one-line local bootstrap surface for daemon + dashboard auth + Telegram owner allowlist setup, and should that live in `openclaw onboard --non-interactive` or a separate bootstrap command?
rationale: The requested behavior is useful and aligned, but it defines a new public setup workflow and security posture for Telegram owner authorization, so maintainer intent is needed before implementation.

options.title: Add explicit allowlist bootstrap
options.body: Expose a narrow setup path that accepts a bot token plus numeric or resolved owner IDs, writes allowlist/preapproval state, and keeps pairing approval explicit for non-owner access.

options.title: Keep flows separate
options.body: Leave `onboard`, `dashboard`, `channels add`, and Telegram config as separate commands, improving docs only for the supported manual composition.

options.title: Defer to external recipes
options.body: Treat the linked external scripted guide as sufficient reference material and keep OpenClaw core focused on the lower-level building blocks.

recommendation.title: Add explicit allowlist bootstrap
recommendation.body: Expose a narrow setup path that accepts a bot token plus numeric or resolved owner IDs, writes allowlist/preapproval state, and keeps pairing approval explicit for non-owner access.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans setup UX, security defaults, and channel ownership boundaries where Peter Steinberger has the strongest combined history signal.
